conviction_note: The print lands into a live, rejected $39 cash bid (Arkhouse / Cobblers Cove, 26 Oct). The bidders have written that they want to talk again once Q3 is out on 4 Nov, and roughly 21% of shares outstanding are short, so downside on a soft quarter is cushioned and a squeeze or a raised-bid headline gives upside. Against that, Applebee's faces a +3.1% comparison while Chili's comped +10.1% over the same months, and H2 needs about +5.6% y/y adjusted EBITDA just to reach the low end of the $220-230M guide. Findings net to +0.6; p_up is 54 on a 5.0% absolute move, so the scaled number is +0.4, close to zero because the two sides are both real.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS consensus $1.07 and revenue $246.8M (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-10-27, https://finviz.com/news/409047/dine-brands-needs-applebees-to-stop-sliding-as-company-owned-bet-squeezes-cash). Benzinga shows about $1.06 / $241.8M (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/DIN/earnings-forecasts), so two sources agree on EPS. Chartmill is lower at $0.97 / $242.1M (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/DIN/estimates). Company FY2026 guide, reiterated at Q1 and maintained at Q2: Applebee's comps 0% to 2%, IHOP comps 0% to 2%, adjusted EBITDA about $220-230M, G&A $205-210M, capex $25-35M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000049754/000119312526207550/d151134dex991.htm). On the Q2 call the CFO said the company is 'maybe towards the lower end of the guidance' (https://www.webull.com.au/news-detail/15390590975501312). Revenue is the line used for print_vs_bar_pct; the EBITDA guide is the line the stock is most likely to trade on.
positioning_check: Short interest (equibles.com, FINRA settlements, https://equibles.com/stocks/din/shortinterest): 2,729,394 shares on 2026-10-15, 4.27 days to cover. That compares with 2,257,432 on 09-30, 1,843,291 on 09-15 and 1,549,589 on 08-31, so it rose about 76% into the bid. The page puts it at 21.6% of 12.66M shares outstanding; percent of free float is higher but not reported. The 10-31 settlement, the first after the bid, is not yet published. Skew: none. The front chain is unusable (ATM legs not two-sided), and put/call OI is 0.09 on only 769 contracts, so the option market makes no directional statement. Tape: +9.5% over 5 days and +18.7% over 20 days. Spot is $35.05 against the $39 non-binding bid, a roughly 10% gap. The unaffected close was $32.01 on 10-27 (Restaurant Dive) or $31.10 on 10-23 (bid letter). This is a crowded short facing a takeover floor.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-26 Arkhouse and Cobblers Cove made a non-binding offer of $39.00 cash per share: no financing condition, equity committed at signing, whole-business-securitization debt with a committed bridge, and an open door to raising the price after diligence. The board rejected it on 10-29 as 'substantially undervalued' and adopted a 10%/20% rights plan expiring 2027-10-27. On 11-02 the bidders wrote that they want to discuss the proposal and a possible higher price 'once you have announced your third quarter earnings on November 4'. Spot is $35.05, about 10% under the bid and about 9.5% over the unaffected $32.01, so the print day is the first time the board's standalone case and the bidders' next move meet in public.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior bid in the baseline's seven prints (median absolute move 3.41%, max 6.42%). The bid itself moved the stock from $32.01 (10-27 close) to about $35-36. Arkhouse's last public bid, for Macy's, ended in July 2024 when Macy's cited a lack of financing certainty, and Macy's fell sharply on that news (https://www.nbcnews.com/business/business-news/macys-ends-buyout-talks-arkhouse-brigade-months-negotiations-rcna161992). That history is the reason the stock trades 10% below $39.
findings.why_not_priced: The bid is public and priced as a probability, not a certainty: a 10% gap to $39 on a name that has never been bid for. What is not priced is how the print shifts that probability. A soft Applebee's quarter or a cut to the low end of the EBITDA guide weakens the board's 'substantially undervalued' rejection and strengthens the bidders, who have dated their re-engagement to this release. A strong quarter lifts the standalone value. Either way the unaffected price ($31-32) is unlikely to be the anchor again within one session. If the market had priced the bid as dead, spot would sit near $32. If it had priced it as done, spot would sit near $38-39.
findings.independence: The 8-K (Item 8.01, signed 2026-11-03) confirms the proposal and the rejection: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000049754/000119312526444401/d146714d8k.htm. Restaurant Dive (2026-10-30) covers the rights plan and Bloomberg's report that the group has economic exposure to almost 20% of shares through swaps: https://www.restaurantdive.com/news/dine-brands-poison-pill-acquisition-offer-ihop-applebees/873213/. The 13D (primary_doc) shows only about 5.7% held as shares (Cobblers 1.4% plus Arkhouse 546,700 shares), so the 20% swap figure is Bloomberg's, not a filing.

findings.finding: FINRA short interest was 2,729,394 shares on the 2026-10-15 settlement, before the bid surfaced: 21.6% of 12.66M shares outstanding and 4.27 days to cover, up from 1,549,589 on 08-31. Those shorts are now positioned against a $39 cash floor-and-ceiling story. Any print, call remark or bidder statement on 11-04 that keeps the bid alive forces further covering in a stock that trades about 650k shares a day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior squeeze is visible in the baseline. The +9.5% five-day run-up after the 10-28 Bloomberg report is consistent with partial covering, but the 10-31 settlement that would show it is unpublished.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is published with a lag. The last published number predates the bid, so how much covering has already happened is unknown. If the shorts had fully covered, the 5-day run-up would be larger and spot closer to the bid; at a 10% gap, about 2.7M shares (roughly 4 days of volume) may still be short into the print.
findings.independence: curvedtrading carries the same 09-15 (1.8M, 5.7 days) and 09-30 (2.26M, 3.4 days) rows per the search snippet: https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/din/short-interest/. Same FINRA source, so not independent of it.

findings.finding: Applebee's faces its toughest comparison of the year in Q3: +3.1% domestic comps in Q3 2025 (company release). Brinker reported on 2026-10-28, after Dine last spoke, that Chili's, Applebee's most direct casual-dining rival, comped +10.1% with +6.4% traffic over the quarter ended 2026-09-23. Applebee's comps have gone +3.1%, +1.9%, then -1.8% (Q2 2026, traffic down), and YTD it sits near 0% against a 0-2% FY guide. A second negative Applebee's quarter is the plausible print, and the Earnings Whispers preview names it as the test.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Applebee's comps drive this stock. The 2025-08-06 print fell 6.42% and the 2026-05-06 print fell 3.52% (Applebee's +1.9% but EBITDA down). The 2026-08-05 print, Applebee's -1.8% with EPS and revenue beats and guide held, rose 2.58%, so a known-weak Applebee's comp has been looked through when the guide held.
findings.why_not_priced: Applebee's Q3 comp has no published consensus (the preview gives none), and the peer read-through came after Dine's last update. The market has focused on the bid since 10-28, the same day Brinker reported. Had the read-through been priced, DIN would have lagged on Brinker's day; instead it rose on the bid report.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 comparison base: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/49754/000119312525265665/d10586dex991.htm. Q2 2026 traffic decline from the 10-Q: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000049754/000162828026052924/din-20260628.htm. This is a proxy: Chili's taking share is an inference, not an Applebee's number, and the broader Black Box series (separate finding) points the other way.

findings.finding: Darden's FQ1 FY27 call (2026-09-24) cited the Black Box casual-dining benchmark excluding Darden, calendar-aligned to June-August 2026, at +2.4% same-restaurant sales and -0.2% guest counts. That is a materially better industry backdrop than the traffic declines Applebee's reported for Q2, and it covers two of the three months in Dine's Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Applebee's has lagged Black Box in recent quarters (Q2 traffic down while management said only IHOP beat the benchmark), so industry strength has not reliably transmitted.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an industry series, public since September, and no Dine-specific transmission is confirmed. It is filed small because it is the broader series the Chili's proxy has to be weighed against.
findings.independence: The Benzinga transcript confirms the benchmark definition: https://www.benzinga.com/node/61971635. It is a proxy for Applebee's, and it includes Chili's strength, so it partly overlaps the previous finding in the opposite direction.

findings.finding: EBITDA guide arithmetic from the company's own releases. H1 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $105.0M ($50.8M + $54.2M) against $110.9M in H1 2025. FY2025 was $219.8M, which implies H2 2025 of $108.9M (Q3 $49.0M). The low end of the reiterated $220-230M guide therefore needs H2 2026 of about $115M, roughly +5.6% y/y after a -5.3% first half. H1 adjusted free cash flow was $3.7M against $48.7M, and Applebee's commodity inflation was running +8.2% on beef. A cut to the low end, or below it, is the likely guidance line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-05-06 print (EBITDA $50.8M vs $54.7M, guide reiterated) fell 3.52%. The 2025-08-06 print fell 6.42%. A held guide in August bought +2.58%.
findings.why_not_priced: The CFO already flagged 'toward the lower end', so a narrowing to about $220M is largely expected. That is why this is sized small. What is not priced is a cut below $220M. A board that has just called $39 'substantially undervalued' has an incentive not to cut, which pulls this toward zero. A bid-anchored price also mutes the reaction to a standalone guide cut.
findings.independence: FY2025 $219.8M and the guide range: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000049754/000119312526207550/d151134dex991.htm. Q3 2025 $49.0M: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/49754/000119312525265665/d10586dex991.htm. CFO remark: https://www.webull.com.au/news-detail/15390590975501312. All are company documents; the arithmetic is mine.

findings.finding: IHOP has an easy Q3 comparison (-1.5% in Q3 2025). It comped +1.5% in Q2 2026, its third straight quarter ahead of the Black Box benchmark on sales and traffic, and on the 2026-08-05 call management said 'early Q3 trends suggest that momentum is continuing' and that the Dubai Chocolate Pancakes LTO was running above expectations. A positive IHOP comp at or above the 0-2% guide is likely and offsets part of Applebee's weakness.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-08-05 print, with IHOP +1.5% and outperforming, rose 2.58%. IHOP has been the offset that holds up the multiple when Applebee's is soft.
findings.why_not_priced: The call commentary has been public since August. The easy comparison is arithmetic nobody needs to aggregate, but there is no consensus for IHOP comps, so the size of the beat on this line is open. First Watch, the nearest daytime peer, reported on 11-03 (after Dine last spoke): comps +1.0% with traffic -1.9%, and it raised its FY outlook. That is a mixed category read, so this finding stays small.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 IHOP -1.5%: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/49754/000119312525265665/d10586dex991.htm. First Watch Q3 2026: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001789940/000178994026000098/exhibit991q32026.htm (a peer, mixed signal). The call transcript is shared with the EBITDA finding's CFO remark.

findings.finding: Cash generation has collapsed. H1 2026 adjusted free cash flow was $3.7M against $48.7M a year earlier, unrestricted cash fell from $104.2M to $97.5M by Q2-end, and $29M of buybacks were done YTD, while the company-operated base has grown to 136 units (including 48 Applebee's taken back in June). The bid letter's price assumes 'net debt consistent with public filings', so a weak Q3 cash line touches both the standalone case and the bid terms.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separately visible in the baseline. The Q2 print, with weak H1 FCF, still rose 2.58%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and flagged in the 10-27 preview, so it is largely priced. It is filed small because Q3 FCF is unforecast and the bid adds a new reason the line matters.
findings.independence: The Earnings Whispers preview repeats the FCF figures, the 136 company units and the 8.2% beef inflation: https://finviz.com/news/409047/dine-brands-needs-applebees-to-stop-sliding-as-company-owned-bet-squeezes-cash. Same company figures, not independent.

outside_window.finding: SSCP-affiliated Applebee's franchisees (Apple Texas and Apple Houston) are suing in federal court in Kansas (filed 2026-03-19, amended 04-17) to stop dual-brand development in their exclusive territories, and Applebee's has countersued over their Logan's Roadhouse purchase. No ruling is dated inside the window. The case bears on the dual-brand plan (80 units by year-end, up to 900 over a decade).

The bidders put diligence at 4 to 6 weeks and a definitive agreement at 6 to 8 weeks after access. Any signed deal resolves well after 2026-11-04; only the re-engagement step can land inside the window.

baseline_tension: The +18.7% 20-day run-up is the bid, not priced earnings optimism, and with no usable skew there is no option-market directional statement to fight. The fundamental negatives (Applebee's against Chili's, the EBITDA guide arithmetic) cut against the run-up, but they meet a 21%-short stock anchored by a $39 bid whose authors have dated their next move to this release, so they are shrunk and p_up sits only slightly above 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short, 21.6% of shares outstanding): shrank the Applebee's/Chili's negative from -1.0 to -0.7 and the FCF negative from -0.3 to -0.2.
Lesson 6 (a finding inside what the company already guided): the CFO already said 'toward the lower end', so the EBITDA guide finding moved from -1.0 to -0.6.
Lesson 5 (a narrow proxy against a broad series): kept the Chili's share-take finding small and labelled it a proxy; kept the Black Box +2.4% series beside it at +0.3.

Lesson 1 (the reaction function): a known-weak Applebee's comp with the guide held bought +2.58% in August, so the reported-quarter negatives stay small. p_up moved from 53 to 54 as the negatives shrank.
Lessons 6 and 8: the bar is sourced to two agreeing estimates ($1.06-1.07), so no cap applies; abs_move_pct is held at 5.0, above the 3.41 median, for the bid and the short.
Bid (+0.5), short-squeeze (+0.8), Black Box (+0.3) and IHOP (+0.5) left standing.
